source.title: xTrimoPGLM: unified 100-billion-parameter pretrained transformer for deciphering the language of proteins
source.authors: Bo Chen; Xingyi Cheng; Pan Li; Yangli-ao Geng; Jing Gong; Shen Li; Zhi-Lei Bei; Xu Tan; Boyan Wang; Xin Zeng; Chiming Liu; Ao-Han Zeng; Yu-Xiao Dong; Jie Tang; Le Song

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some figure and table extraction has OCR corruption, but the text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper investigates scaling in protein language models, a new modality relative to the original language-model scaling studies. Its tests are protein-specific and do not reproduce the original held-out-loss measurement or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper fits training-loss scaling against compute for xTrimoPGLM models trained with a fixed token count, and compares that fit with a much larger model. It also reports downstream scaling results. The OOD perplexity comparisons between xTrimoPGLM-100B, ESM2-15B and PROGEN2-xlarge are not scaling sweeps, so they are not cataloged as scaling-law rows. Values used only to configure training are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: In protein language models, the study fits a power law of pretraining loss against compute across xTrimoPGLM models from 1M to 1B parameters at 100B tokens. It says the fit matches the 100B model, and it reports downstream performance across model sizes (230M to 100B) and across pretraining checkpoints against MLM validation loss. These are a new modality's own results on V2, V5 and V6. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say xTrimoPGLM loss follows a power law in compute, fitted on 1M–1B models, that matches the 100B model. They say downstream performance rises roughly linearly with log pretraining compute, with task-dependent shapes: 44% gradual, 28% Grokking, 16% non-linear and 12% inverse scaling. Missing from the record's paraphrase: zero-shot fitness does not improve with scale, and OOD structure prediction shows diminishing returns.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits training loss against compute approximated as 6ND, using protein models and a fixed token count for the smaller-model fit, then compares with a larger model. It does not reproduce the original held-out-loss measurement, and it does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports task-dependent downstream scaling, including gradual gains, Grokking, non-linear patterns and inverse scaling. Its main pretraining-loss fit holds training tokens fixed for the smaller models; no alternative fitting methods or fitting choices are compared.

fits_no_version.finding: The 100B model reaches lower OOD perplexity than ESM2-15B and PROGEN2-xlarge with fewer trained tokens; the authors read this as larger models being more sample-efficient. This is a cross-family comparison, not a controlled sweep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger protein LMs reach a given held-out perplexity with fewer training tokens.

record.code_released: https://huggingface.co/proteinglm (trained weights and downstream datasets are stated to be available; source code release is not stated)
record.problems: The scaling-loss fit is reported for training loss rather than held-out loss. The larger-model comparison has no numerical prediction error, and the main text/figure extraction does not provide the underlying loss points or uncertainty. Token-count descriptions for the larger model are inconsistent. Downstream results are task-specific; several show non-monotonic behavior. Supplementary Table 6 reports some training-FLOP values that are non-monotonic or repeated across sizes.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining fixed-model downstream benchmark comparisons (including Supplementary Tables 3–5) and OOD perplexity model comparisons were not extracted as scaling-sweep rows; the controlled xTrimoPGLM size sweep in Supplementary Table 6 and the training-state aggregates in Figure 2C were retained. No results were omitted from Supplementary Table 6 or the four reported Figure 2C task-group percentages.

untested.parts: Text-LM held-out loss is not studied. The protein-LM power-law fit is treated under V5.
There is no numerical extrapolation error, and no held-out-loss extrapolation.
There is no compute-optimal N/D sweep; the Discussion only advocates proportional scaling.
There is no depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count.
Only protein sequences are tested, with D fixed. Images, video, repeated data and fine-tuning are not tested as scaling settings.
There is no fitted predictive law from loss to task, and no held-out prediction of downstream scores.
Fitting choices, schedules and parameter counting are not varied.

missing.what: Zero-shot ProteinGym fitness Spearman across xT1B, 3B, 10B and 100B (0.4067, 0.4192, 0.4176, 0.3987), plus the ESM2 and PROGEN2 size series. The authors state that scaling does not hold for zero-shot fitness.
missing.locator: Supplementary Table 7; Zero-shot Fitness Prediction paragraph

missing.what: Supervised GB1 LoRA fine-tuning across xT1B, 3B, 10B and 100B (0.9577, 0.9542, 0.9624, 0.9610), which is flat and non-monotonic. The linear-probe values are 0.7690 to 0.8169.

Category-mean downstream performance against log PF-days across ESM2-150M, 650M, 3B, 15B and xT100B, with linear-in-log fits for probing and LoRA. Example: Structure probing y = 5.104x + 56.090, LoRA y = 4.261x + 68.927.
missing.locator: Figure 2B; Comparison Between ESM and xTrimoPGLM Family models

missing.what: A qualitative statement of diminishing returns for OOD (CASP15) structure prediction as the PLM scales. The cited Figure 1D is not in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The per-step D rows compare each size only with the next smaller one. A per-task whole-sweep row would be clearer. Several increments are under 1 point and no uncertainty is reported. Sizes in Supplementary Table 6 have non-monotonic or tied FLOPs, and unstated token counts, so 'scale' mixes size, data and compute. Task-group membership for C1–C4 is read from a garbled figure.

versions.untested_parts: The paper discusses cross-entropy test loss, but its scaling fit uses training losses; it does not test held-out pretraining loss falling as a power law across parameters, tokens or compute.
Tests a fit from smaller protein models against a larger model for training loss, not held-out loss; the text does not provide a numerical prediction error.
No sweep finds the loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation for fixed compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests protein sequence modeling with fixed-token training-loss scaling; does not test images, video, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning or transfer as scaling-law settings.

Tests downstream performance across xTrimoPGLM model sizes on eight tasks and reports task-performance relationships with MLM validation loss. It does not establish predictable scaling for all downstream tasks or all model families.
Does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, data or fitting method to test their effect on fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: xTrimoPGLM-series models (1 million to 1 billion parameters; aggregate fit)
rows.operation_detail: Fit training loss against compute, with compute approximated as 6ND and training tokens fixed at 100 billion for these models.
rows.measure: Training loss versus compute; the paper describes a power-law fit and says the curve aligns closely with the 100-billion-parameter model’s training loss.
rows.locator: Quantification Scaling Law of xTrimoPGLM Family Models; Figure 1C
rows.note: The figure includes the fit expression “L = 2.63 * C 0.017”; the extracted rendering does not clearly establish the exponent sign. The text states that the fitted curve aligns closely with the larger model. The measured quantity is training loss, not held-out loss.
rows.check: This is the fit that S2's comparison relies on, so it should be linked to V2 (this clears the reader's label-link issue). The value is figure-only. The extracted exponent lost its sign and is almost certainly C^-0.017, since the authors describe loss falling. D is fixed at 100B tokens, so the fit is effectively L(N) at fixed data, not compute-optimal L(C). The text calls it training loss; the figure axis reads 'Test loss'. No fit quality is given.

source_check.locator_found: Quantification Scaling Law, lines 428–444; Figure 1C. Embedded equation metadata confirms L=2.63*C^(-0.017).

source_check.condition: Linear-probing tasks rising monotonically with size (contact, fitness, solubility); checkpoint tasks rising gradually
source_check.reason: Supplementary Table 6 confirms monotonic size trends for these tasks, and the checkpoint section reports 44% gradual improvement. Some individual increments are small; this supports conditional trends rather than a validated forecasting law.

relationships.condition: Tasks that improve overall but non-monotonically or abruptly (fold, fluorescence, localization, metal binding; Grokking and non-linear checkpoint tasks)
relationships.reason: These tasks dip at 650M or 10B before rising at 100B (D8–D12, D14–D18, D26–D30, D32–D36). Against pretraining loss, 28% of tasks show Grokking and 16% are not strictly linear (C2, C3).

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Tasks that improve overall but non-monotonically or abruptly (fold, fluorescence, localization, metal binding; Grokking and non-linear checkpoint tasks)
source_check.reason: Supplementary Table 6 confirms intermediate size reversals despite overall gains; the checkpoint section reports 28% Grokking and 16% non-linear patterns. Abruptness or nonlinearity alone does not establish unpredictability.

relationships.condition: Stability probing, inverse-scaling checkpoint tasks, and zero-shot fitness

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Protein LM; fit on 1M–1B xTrimoPGLM models at 100B tokens, compared with the 100B model at the same token count
labels.reason: The scaling section explicitly reports close alignment with the 100B model at the same token count; no numerical prediction error is reported.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Protein sequence pretraining (MLM-stage loss), fixed 100B tokens, 1M–1B parameters
labels.reason: Figure 1C and the scaling section report a protein pretraining power law. The embedded equation metadata confirms the negative exponent, -0.017.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Linear-probing tasks rising monotonically with size (contact, fitness, solubility); checkpoint tasks rising gradually
labels.reason: Supplementary Table 6 confirms monotonic size trends for these tasks, and the checkpoint section reports 44% gradual improvement. Some individual increments are small; this supports conditional trends rather than a validated forecasting law.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Tasks that improve overall but non-monotonically or abruptly (fold, fluorescence, localization, metal binding; Grokking and non-linear checkpoint tasks)
labels.reason: Supplementary Table 6 confirms intermediate size reversals despite overall gains; the checkpoint section reports 28% Grokking and 16% non-linear patterns. Abruptness or nonlinearity alone does not establish unpredictability.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Stability probing, inverse-scaling checkpoint tasks, and zero-shot fitness
labels.reason: Stability decreases 80.10→78.36→75.52 across 3B→10B→100B; 12% of checkpoint tasks show inverse scaling. Supplementary Table 7 gives zero-shot fitness 0.4192 at 3B versus 0.3987 at 100B, and the authors explicitly report failure of scaling there.

relation.reason: The study measures whether power-law loss scaling, extrapolation and downstream improvements hold in its protein models.

tranche.reason: Protein sequence pretraining is a new setting with its own loss-scaling fit, larger-model comparison and downstream scaling results.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is the December 2024 arXiv version, not the final journal text. The 100B-token comparison can use an intermediate checkpoint of the 1T-token run; those counts are compatible. Figure 7 lists non-monotonic compute across sizes, including identical compute for 3B and 10B.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Protein-model training-loss fit from smaller xTrimoPGLM models compared with xTrimoPGLM-100B
reader_labels.reason: The authors report close alignment between the fitted curve and the larger model’s actual training loss (S1–S2); no numerical error is given.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Protein sequence models; xTrimoPGLM family fit at fixed 100-billion-token training for the smaller models
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports a power-law fit of protein-model training loss against compute and alignment with a larger model (S1–S2); this does not establish the form in other modalities or regimes.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Downstream linear-probing tasks with generally rising performance across xTrimoPGLM sizes
reader_labels.reason: Most task sweeps rise with size, including contact, fitness, solubility and several other tasks (D1–D6, D19–D24, D37–D42). The authors also report gradual increases for 44% of tasks in the training-state analysis (C1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Downstream tasks with nonlinear patterns, size-specific dips or inverse scaling
reader_labels.reason: The authors report Grokking for 28%, non-strictly-linear behavior for 16%, and potential inverse scaling for 12% of tasks (C2–C4); fold, fluorescence, localization, metal-binding and stability sweeps also include decreases at some sizes (D7–D18, D25–D36, D43–D48).
